tested_scope: Primary-source verification of GitHub repository Contents REST API as lightweight checkpoint/evidence transport only. This slice does not test hosted compute, GitHub Actions, Codespaces, model execution, or end-to-end scheduled-Chat parity.

primary_sources.observed: The create-or-update contents endpoint creates/replaces repository files, requires the current file sha when updating, and documents 200/201 success plus 409 conflict behavior. Fine-grained tokens can use repository Contents write permission; Workflows permission is additionally relevant only for workflow-file changes.
GitHub REST API requests are rate-limited on an hourly basis; the documented authenticated-user baseline is 5,000 requests/hour, with other token classes having their own hourly limits.

verification.finite_monthly_trial_paid_quota_dependen: not_established; primary evidence instead shows hourly REST rate limits
verification.zero_quota_rate_limit_resilience: not_proven_here; must be supplied by cross-invocation checkpoint/resume behavior

reason: The primary source supports repository Contents API as a serializable, sha-bound state/evidence transport with explicit conflict behavior, and it does not require Actions or Codespaces for ordinary contents writes. But an hourly REST rate limit exists, this slice does not establish universal zero incremental cost, and it does not prove model/execution parity. Therefore it may support a checkpoint transport subcomponent only; it cannot close a dependency-elimination row or ancestor by itself.
continuation: Verify one concrete current Phase-1 route that actually uses repository checkpoint transport: bind its exact candidate identity and evidence, then test whether the route survives an injected REST rate-limit or missing-write-surface condition across invocations without duplicate effects, without Actions/Codespaces/artifact compute, without residual Work/protected/user execution, and with zero incremental cost. Do not treat transport capability alone as parity acceptance.
